source.citation: National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON). Discrete-return LiDAR (DP1.30003.001), Elevation LiDAR (DP3.30024.001), and Site management and event reporting (DP1.10111.001), Soaproot Saddle tutorial cohort.
source.license: CC BY 4.0 for NEON data products; tutorial repository code is AGPL-3.0

selection.releaseBoundary: The official tutorial bundle is pinned by exact public file IDs and bytes; it is not relabelled as a formal NEON release.

publishedInterpretation.claim: The tutorial identifies the selected 2019 and 2021 SOAP LiDAR tile as a small fire-affected area observed before and after the 2020 Creek Fire.

eventGroup.label: Creek Fire / four rendered source records

beforeAfter.interpretation: Most matched cells have lower projected height quantiles in 2021, but the comparison is descriptive because the LiDAR sensor changed and no causal design is present.

similarSnapshot.interpretation: The same 10 m cell has the same four-value signature at 0.1 m display precision before and after the selected recorded event, but the event context and measurement protocol differ.

historyEquivalence.reason: The pair refers to one exact 10 m grid cell.
All four displayed height quantiles agree at 0.1 m precision.
The unrounded quantiles and retained-return counts differ.
The 2021 observation follows the selected Creek Fire records; the 2019 observation does not.
The surveys used different LiDAR sensors.
The four-variable projection cannot decide full ecosystem identity.

historicalLoad.reason: No finite ecological route space, route-cost function, or history-free baseline is defined; undefined must not be displayed as zero.

nonClaims: The four height quantiles are not the full ecosystem state.
The recorded Creek Fire is not a causal-effect estimate.
The event records do not define an exact fire perimeter for the LiDAR tile.
The two surveys do not form a recovery trajectory.
A rounded equal state signature is not ecosystem identity.
A rounded equal state signature is not history identity.
The 2019 and 2021 sensors are not interchangeable protocols.
Missing event records do not prove that no disturbance occurred.
No future ecological state is predicted.
Historical Load is undefined rather than zero.
